title: I Turned My Tiny Balcony Into a Vegetable Garden
creator: Omar Haddad
description:
Four square meters, fourteen containers, and more tomatoes than I can eat.

Thanks to Quietly for sponsoring! Code BALCONY gets you 20% off at https://quietly.audio

What I grow: cherry tomatoes, chillies, basil, lettuce, beans, strawberries.
Compost video: linked in the end screen.

sentences.t: Six months ago, this balcony was just the place where I kept a broken chair.
Today it grows about half of the vegetables I eat in summer.
Quick thank you to Quietly for sponsoring this video.

Okay, so let me show you around, which will take about four seconds, because this balcony is four square meters.
The big lesson from this whole project is that on a small balcony you have to grow up, not out.
So along this wall I put up a cheap trellis, and the beans and the cucumbers climb right up it.
On the railing I've got these hanging planters, and that's all herbs, basil, parsley, thyme, and a mint that is trying to take over the world.
Always put mint in its own pot, by the way, or it will strangle everything else.
Then on the floor, the big containers, and these are the stars of the show.
Cherry tomatoes, three plants, in pots that are about forty liters each.
My first year I used tiny pots and the tomatoes were sad and miserable, so bigger is really better here.
Look at this, these are ripening right now, and they taste nothing like the ones from the supermarket.
Over here are the chillies, which absolutely love the heat coming off the wall.
This balcony faces south, so it gets sun from about ten in the morning until five, which is the dream for vegetables.
If yours faces north, don't give up, just stick to lettuce, spinach, and herbs that like a bit of shade.
Watering is the hardest part, honestly.
In July I was out here twice a day, with containers drying out by lunchtime.
So I set up a really simple drip system from a water barrel and a little timer, and it changed my life.
It cost about thirty euros and now I can actually go away for a weekend.
For soil I mix potting compost with some of my own compost from the kitchen scraps bin I've got in the corner.
No smell, I promise, if you get the mix of greens and browns right.
And then the strawberries, in this tower planter, which my neighbor's kid steals from every afternoon.
I pretend I don't see her.
So what did I actually harvest this year?
About eleven kilos of tomatoes, a ridiculous amount of beans, salad leaves pretty much every day from May to September, and enough chillies to make hot sauce for everyone I know.
Not bad for a space where I used to keep a broken chair.
In the next video I'll show you how I start everything from seed on my windowsill in February.
Thanks for watching, and happy growing.
